questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India is related to the Uniform Civil Code for the citizens?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 44**__.

__
 
• **Article 44 of the Constitution of India is related to the Uniform Civil Code for the citizens**__.

__
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**

 
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are described in Articles 36 to 51 in Part IV of the Constitution.
 
• They embody the concept of a welfare state.
 
• DPSPs are fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• DPSPs are non-equitable.
 
• They apply to the Union and State Governments and all other authorities falling within the definition of 'State'.
 
• This is a feature borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland.
 
• **Article 44:** To secure a uniform civil code for all citizens throughout the country.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 42**: To make provision for just and humane conditions for work and maternity relief.
 
• **Article 45**: To provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.
 
• **Article 40**: To organize village Panchayat of function as units of self-government.

questions.question: Who among the following has the power to nominate some members in the Legislative Council of a state?

options.text: The Governor of the concerned state
The Chief Minister of the concerned state
The Chairman of the Legislative Council of the concerned state

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Governor of the concerned state**__.

__
 
• **The Governor of the concerned state has the power to nominate some members in the Legislative Council of a state**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Legislative Council of a state:**

 
 
• As per** Article 169**, if the Legislative Assembly passes a resolution for abolishing or creating of the Legislative Council by a majority of the total membership of the Assembly and by a** majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting,** the Parliament may approve the resolution by a simple majority to create or abolish the Legislative Council.
 
• The size of the Legislative Council may vary, but its membership** should not be more than 1/3rd of the membership of the Legislative Assembly but not less than 40**.
 
• **5/6th of the total number of members of the Council is indirectly elected** and **1/6th is nominated by the Governor**.
 
• Of the total number of members of a Legislative Council:
 
 
• **1/3rd** elected from** local bodies (municipalities and district boards).**
 
• **1/12th** elected by **graduates of 3 years standing and residing in the state.**
 
• **1/12th **elected by** teachers of 3 years standing in the State, not lower in standing than secondary school.**
 
• **1/3rd** elected by the **members of the Legislative Assembly of the State** from amongst persons, who are not members of the assembly.
 
• **Rest (1/6th) **are** nominated by the Governor** from a **person of special knowledge or practical experience of literature, science, art, co-operative movement and social service.**

questions.question: Tiny pores present on the surface of leaves are known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**stomata**__.

__
 
• **Tiny pores present on the surface of leaves are known as stomata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stomata:**

 
 
• Stomata are small pores present in the epidermis of leaves, stems and other plant parts.
 
• The stomata are surrounded by two guard cells.
 
• This allows gases such as carbon dioxide, water vapor and oxygen to diffuse into and out of the plant's internal tissues.
 
• It occurs mostly in vascular plants.
 
• The inner wall of the guard cell is thicker than the outer wall.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nucleus**

 
 
• It was discovered by **Robert Brown**.
 
• The nucleus is **rich in protein** and **RNA**.
 
• **Chromatin **is the controlling **center of a cell.**
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria:**
 
 
• It is a **semi-autonomous organelle** and called the **powerhouse **of the cell because in it stepwise oxidation of fuel occurs which results in a release of chemical energy.
 
• This **energy is stored in the form of ATP.**
 
 
 
• The **cytoplasm **is the fluid found **outside the nuclear membrane.**

questions.question: What was the name of King Ashoka’s daughter whom he appointed to carry out the duties of a Buddhist missionary?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanghamitra**__.

__
 
• **Sanghamitra was King Ashoka’s daughter was appointed to carry out the duties of a Buddhist missionary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Ashoka (273 BC-232 BC):**

 
 
• He was the greatest Mauryan ruler, Governor of Taxila and Ujjain.
 
• His rule extended to the whole of the sub-continent except the extreme south.
 
 
• It also included **Afghanistan, Baluchistan, Kashmir and the valleys of Nepal.**
 
 
 
• Ashoka had himself formally crowned in **269 BC.**
 
• Under Ashoka, the **Mauryan Empire reached its climax.**
 
• Ashoka fought the Kalinga War in **261 BC** in the 8th year of his coronation.
 
 
• Later, he was moved by the massacre in this war and, therefore, abandoned the policy of physical occupation in favour of the policy of cultural conquest.
 
• **Bherighosa was replaced by Dhammaghosa.**
 
 
 
• He embraced Buddhism under** Upagupta.**
 
• He sent his son ***Mahendra ***and daughter ***Sanghamitra*** to** Ceylon** (Sri Lanka as Buddhist missionaries with a sapling of original peepal tree).
 
• He inaugurated Dhamma Yatras from the 11th year of his reign by visiting Bodh Gaya and also appointed*** Dhamma Mahamatras*** (officer of righteousness to spread the message of Dhamma).

questions.question: In order to curb the East India Company traders’ unrestrained commercial activities and to bring about some order in territories under the Company control, the British Parliament enacted a series of laws among which the _______ stood first.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Regulating Act of 1773**__.

__
 
• **In order to curb the unrestrained business activities of the East India Company's merchants and to bring some order in the areas under the control of the Company, the British Parliament enacted a series of laws, the first of which was the Regulation Act of 1773**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Regulating Act of 1773**

 
 
• Governance of the East India Company was put under British parliamentary control.
 
• The Governor of Bengal was nominated as **Governor-General for all the three Presidencies of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras.**
 
• **Warren Hastings** was the first such **Governor-General.**
 
• A** Supreme Court** was established in **Calcutta **(now Kolkata).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Charter Act of 1813:**

 
 
• The trade monopoly of the East India Company came to an end.
 
• The Christian Missionaries were allowed to spread their religion in India.
 
 
 
• **Charter Act of 1833:**
 
 
• The **Governor-General** and his council were given vast powers.
 
• The council had absolute powers with respect to revenue, and a single budget for the country was prepared by the governor-general.
 
• For the first time, the Governor-General's government was known as the '**Government of India' and his council as the 'Indian Council'**.
 
• The Governor-General of Bengal was to be the Governor-General of India.
 
• All powers, administrative and financial, **were delegated to the Governor-General in Council**.
 
• A Law Commission was set up under Lord Macaulay for the codification of laws.

questions.question: Proboscis gland for excretion is present in the phylum:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hemichordata**__.

__
 
• **The probosci's gland for excretion is present in the Hemichordata phylum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hemichordata**:

 
 
• It is a phylum of **marine invertebrates.**
 
• They are found in a wide range of** depths and habitats in the oceans.**
 
• The body is mainly divided into three parts:** proboscis (protostome), collar (mesosome) and trunk (metasome).**
 
• They show all the characteristics of **Deuterostomia **and at least one unique structure i.e. the stomochord which is a cartilaginous element that projects into the protocoel and supports the heart and kidney complex. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phylum Mollusca:**

 
 
• The body is divided into the head and muscular foot.
 
• The mantle is always present in it.
 
• The alimentary canal is well developed.
 
• Respiration takes place through gills or ctenidia.
 
• Blood is colourless.
 
• Excretion takes place through the kidneys.
 
• Example: Pila, Octopus.
 
 
 
• **Phylum Arthropoda**
 
 
• The body is divided into three parts– Head, Thorax and Abdomen.
 
• The body is covered with a thick chitinous exoskeleton.
 
• Jointed leg.
 
• The circulatory system is of open type.
 
• Its body cavities are called haemocoels.
 
• The trachea, book lungs, body surface are respiratory parts.
 
• These are mainly unisexual and fertilization takes place inside the body.
 
• Example: Cockroach and Prawn.
 
 
 
• **Phylum Porifera:**
 
 
• All animals of this group are found in water and bear pores in the body.
 
• These are multicellular animals but cells do not make regular tissues.
 
• Numerous pores are known as Ostia found on the body wall.
 
• Skeleton is made up of minute calcareos or silicon spicules.
 
• Examples: Sycon, Sponge, etc.

questions.question: As per the Constitution of India, the total number of members in the Lok Sabha **CANNOT **be more than:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**552**__.

__
 
• **As per the Constitution of India, the total number of members in the Lok Sabha cannot be more than 552**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Lok Sabha:**

 
 
• It comes under **article 81**
 
• Its **maximum strength is 550 + 2** members of its Anglo-Indian Community, which includes **530 members from States** and **20 from Union Territories**.
 
 
• Now 2 members of the Anglo-Indian Community seat were abolished.
 
 
 
• The **present strength of Lok Sabha is 545.**
 
• The representatives of the States are directly elected by the people of the States on the basis of adult suffrage.
 
• Every citizen who is **not less than 18 years** of age and is not otherwise disqualified is entitled to vote at such an election.
 
• The normal term of the Lok Sabha is 5 years, but it may be dissolved earlier by the President.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajya Sabha:**

 
 
• It comes under** article 80.**
 
• Rajya Sabha is a** permanent body** and not subject to dissolution.
 
• Its** maximum strength is 250.**
 
• The total membership of the** present Rajya Sabha is 245 **however **one-third of members retire every second year.**

questions.question: Which of the following diseases marked by dementia, diarrhoea, and dermatitis, is also known as ‘the three Ds’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pellagra**__.

__
 
• **Pellagra is marked by dementia, diarrhoea, and dermatitis is also known as ‘the three Ds’**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pellagra**:

 
 
• Pellagra is a disease that results due to severe **vitamin B3 (Niacin) deficiency.**
 
• The disease is marked by the result in the **3D’s: diarrhoea, dermatitis, dementia.**
 
 
 
• The disease can also develop due to:
 
 
• Gastrointestinal diseases
 
• Weight loss (bariatric) surgery
 
• Anorexia
 
• Excessive alcohol use
 
• Carcinoid syndrome (group of symptoms associated with tumours of the small intestine, colon, appendix, and bronchial tubes in the lungs).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Osteoporosis **causes bones to become weak and brittle.
 
• ‌**Xerophthalmia **is a disease that causes dry eyes due to **vitamin A deficiency**. 
 
• **Scurvy **is caused due to **vitamin C deficiency**.
 
 
• The disease leads to anaemia, debility, exhaustion, spontaneous bleeding, pain in the limbs, swelling in some parts of the body.

questions.question: Which causative agent causes the disease of malaria?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is a __**parasite**__.

__
 
• **The parasite causes the disease malaria**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Malaria **is a mosquito-borne disease that affects **humans.**

 
 
• The symptoms of this include fever, tiredness, vomiting, and headaches.
 
• The disease can cause yellow skin, seizures, coma, or death.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diseases caused due to bacteria:**

 
 
• Diphtheria, Pneumonia, Cholera, Tetanus, Tuberculosis, Plague and Gonorrhoea.
 
 
 
• **Diseases caused due to Fungi:**
 
 
• **​**Ringworm and Athlete’s Foot.
 
 
 
• **Diseases caused due to Protozoa: **
 
 
• Malaria, dysentery, Diarrhoea, Kala Azar.
 
 
 
• **Diseases caused due to virus:**
 
 
• Small Pox, Chicken Pox, AIDS, Herpes, Dengue, Rabies, Measles, Influenza/Flu
